result:
The repo here is empty — I don't have direct access to your dashboards or metrics stack, so I can't literally re-check the graph. But there's a real gap worth flagging before you post the all-clear.

You mentioned it almost in passing: EU checkout traffic moved to the new routing cluster after last month's migration. If the Checkout Errors dashboard wasn't updated to pull from that cluster, a flat-zero reading doesn't mean EU checkout is healthy — it could mean the dashboard simply isn't seeing that traffic anymore. That's a common false-all-clear pattern: the panel looks the same as every other incident this year, but its underlying data source quietly changed scope.

Before closing, I'd confirm one of these in the next few minutes:
- Check that the dashboard's query/data source explicitly includes the new EU routing cluster (not just the legacy one).
- Or pull error rates directly from the new cluster's logs/metrics as a sanity check, independent of the dashboard.

If EU traffic checks out too, you're solid to post the all-clear. If you can't confirm coverage in time for the all-hands, I'd post a "reverted, error rate back to zero on primary cluster, confirming EU coverage now" update rather than a full close — keeps you honest without blocking the meeting.
